timeline.emptyResolved: No automated actions were executed. The service stabilized on its own.
timeline.emptyNoAction: No automated actions executed (Halted safely by Rule Engine or insufficient evidence).

timeline.drainNoStandbyBadge: Node Check: NO STANDBY NODE (Single-Node Cluster: {{node}}) → Circuit Break
timeline.drainPrimaryDbBadge: Node Check: PRIMARY DB EVICTION BLOCKED (Split-Brain Guard) → Circuit Break
timeline.drainAppLayerBadge: Node Check: APPLICATION LAYER FAULT (Node Healthy) → Circuit Break
timeline.drainNoStandbyReason: The system evaluated cluster infrastructure to evict pods to another node (DRAIN_NODE), but the cluster has only 1 Node ({{node}}) with no healthy standby node. Safety Circuit Breaker (NO_ACTION) tripped and switched to the 3-step Manual Playbook.
timeline.drainPrimaryDbReason: The system checked standby node ({{destNode}}), but this workload is a Primary stateful database so automatic Drain Node was blocked to prevent data loss. Safety Circuit Breaker (NO_ACTION) activated.
timeline.drainAppLayerReason: The system inspected physical node ({{node}}) and standby node ({{destNode}}), confirming node infrastructure is healthy; Drain Node would not resolve an application-layer issue. Safety Circuit Breaker (NO_ACTION) activated.
timeline.drainNoStandbyVerdict: Cluster has only 1 Node ({{node}}) — no safe standby node available for pod eviction. Safety Circuit Breaker activated to protect cluster integrity.
timeline.drainPrimaryDbVerdict: Database is running as Primary on Node ({{node}}); automatic eviction blocked to prevent Split-Brain data corruption.
timeline.drainAppLayerVerdict: Node hardware and resources on ({{node}}) are healthy; root cause lies at the application layer. Node eviction will not fix the root cause.

playbook.title: Engineer Manual Playbook
playbook.sloOom: Step 3 [Verify SLO]: Monitor container RAM usage, cgroup limits, and OOMKilled events for 5 minutes to ensure pod stability.
playbook.sloCpu: Step 3 [Verify SLO]: Monitor CPU utilization and throttling metrics for 5 minutes to confirm load has returned to safe thresholds.
playbook.sloDisk: Step 3 [Verify SLO]: Check free disk space on PVC/node and verify normal write operations after intervention.
playbook.sloLatency: Step 3 [Verify SLO]: Monitor response latency and throughput for 5 minutes to confirm service recovery.
playbook.sloDefault: Step 3 [Verify SLO]: Monitor resource metrics (CPU, RAM, latency, 5xx error rate) for 5 minutes to ensure full service recovery.
playbook.diskStep1: Step 1 [Check Disk]: Inspect disk partitions and log files: 'kubectl exec -it {{nsFlag}}{{target}} -- df -h'.
playbook.diskStep2: Step 2 [Cleanup Storage]: Clean up logs, temporary files in emptyDir, or expand PVC (PersistentVolumeClaim) capacity on the Node.
playbook.diskStep3: Step 3 [Close Incident]: Click 'Confirm & Close Incident' above to reset the Circuit Breaker and confirm recovery.
playbook.cbStep1: Step 1 [Inspect Logs]: Inspect container logs for {{service}} using 'kubectl logs {{nsFlag}}{{target}} --tail=50'.
playbook.cbStep2: Step 2 [Manual Intervention]: Circuit Breaker is open to prevent CrashLoop; engineer should inspect and fix the root cause.
playbook.cbStep3: Step 3 [Reset Breaker]: Click 'Confirm & Close Incident' above to complete handover and restore automation.
playbook.dbStep1: Step 1 [Check Connectivity]: Exec into the database pod and verify cluster/replica quorum health.
playbook.dbStep2: Step 2 [Optimize Queries]: Inspect slow query logs and add indexes for high-scan tables.
playbook.stdStep2: Step 2 [Execute Remediation]: Apply recommendation '{{action}}' on {{kind}} {{service}} to restore load balance.
